lede: Oregon carries the stronger underlying team rating — +9.5 against -0.4, a 9.9-point separation on a neutral field before home advantage, travel or rest.
EdgeDesk makes it Oklahoma State +25.2 before any sportsbook number is consulted, with Oregon winning 95% of simulations.
The position-group comparison shows where the separation comes from: the widest measured gap is continuity, where Oregon leads Oklahoma State by 88 places nationally.
Data confidence on this matchup is 41% — enough to publish, not enough to treat the exact margin as settled.

favourite.heading: Why Oregon can pull away
bullets: Oregon is the better football team by 24.9 points on opponent-adjusted results — but about 86% of that rating is still last season carried forward, and in a portal era last season is a different team (-24.9 pts).
Conference strength differs and the in-season sample is still thin, worth 2.6 points to Oregon (-2.6 pts).

underdog.heading: Why Oklahoma State can keep it close
bullets: Playing at Oklahoma State is worth 4.1 points — the league-wide home-field number, because a per-venue table was tested and could not be told apart from the home team’s own quality (+4.1 pts).
Running backs: Oklahoma State 55.9 (#17 of 101) vs Oregon 55.8 (#21 of 101) — 4 places on the national board.
Defensive line: Oklahoma State 54.2 (#33 of 101) vs Oregon 54.1 (#35 of 101) — 2 places on the national board.
The outcome range is 15.5 points wide at one sigma — p10 -49.2 to p90 -4.2 for Oklahoma State, so a projection of -25.2 still produces results a long way either side of it.
It is early enough that both ratings still lean on preseason belief — it widens the outcome range by about 6%.
